rows.title: Colorado is auditing 1,745 licenses for immigrants driving 18-wheelers, hazardous trucks and buses
rows.standfirst: The state paused its commercial driver’s license program for immigrants with temporary legal status after a new Trump administration rule

rows.title: Swisspod proved the largest hyperloop test facility in the world — in Pueblo — works
rows.standfirst: It will be a long time before tests of the tech being developed in Colorado Springs confirm humans can be shot safely through the tube at 300 mph

rows.title: This Denver sushi counter is one of Esquire’s best new restaurants, and a crowning achievement for its chef
rows.standfirst: The honor comes on top of the Michelin star awarded to chef Toshi Kizaki’s eponymous omakase restaurant in Denver’s Platt Park neighborhood

rows.title: Colorado awarded $420.6M by federal government — nearly half of original grant — for fast rural internet service
rows.standfirst: The state, originally awarded $826.5 million, was forced to redo its BEAD plan to give satellite and wireless a fair chance against the more costly fiber broadband service

rows.title: Delayed return of federal jobs data has some Colorado economists concerned
rows.standfirst: The federal shutdown paused Bureau of Labor Statistics work for six weeks. It’s coming back slowly, though some reports have been cancelled.

rows.title: Xcel can keep Pueblo’s Comanche 2 coal plant open past December as Comanche 3 issues persist
rows.standfirst: An extension was granted by the state Public Utilities Commission to keep the 50-year-old plant open beyond a planned end-of-year deadline, with caveats

rows.title: What’s Working: How a $1.2 million donation is saving a 4-H club in Colorado’s San Luis Valley
rows.standfirst: Do-gooder Larry Brown got the local farm club back in shape. A stranger noticed. Plus: AG settles with Greystar, SecureSavings expands, another Golden moon mission, more!

rows.title: In Colorado town built on coal, some families are moving on, even as Trump tries to boost industry
rows.standfirst: Many countries and about half of U.S. states are moving away from coal, citing environmental impacts and high costs. Burning coal emits carbon dioxide that traps heat in the atmosphere, warming the planet.

rows.title: Can funeral directors operate without licenses in Colorado?
rows.standfirst: Yes. Colorado does not currently require funeral directors and other mortuary science practitioners to have a license to operate in the state.

rows.title: After a chaotic year, experts predict what lies ahead for Colorado’s economy in 2026
rows.standfirst: There’s good news and bad news, but mostly flat news on the state economy front

rows.title: Colorado ranchers say White House beef policy is making a tough job even tougher
rows.standfirst: Ranchers and industry advocates said the Trump administration’s decision to buy more Argentinian beef was particularly damaging because the announcement came during the one time of year when local ranchers sell their cattle

rows.title: Older adults on fixed incomes are finding homeownership in Colorado financially harder than ever
rows.standfirst: The average yearly cost of owning and maintaining a house in Colorado is $25,766, 20% higher than the national average. That doesn’t include the mortgage payment.

rows.title: More data centers are coming to Colorado, demanding more power than they’ll need. Will customers foot the bill?
rows.standfirst: Colorado regulators want rules in place to shield ordinary household and business customers from getting stuck paying for increased generating and transmission capacity

rows.title: $50 million in funding for Denver Summit stadium advanced by City Council committee after deal-threatening delay
rows.standfirst: The decision comes after the women’s soccer team announced they are considering other locations in case delays with the investment continue

rows.title: Planned drill site near Aurora Reservoir delayed by state regulators in a win for neighborhood group
rows.standfirst: Crestone Peak Resources, which has met opposition from the grassroots Save the Aurora Reservoir, must look for an alternative location farther from homes

rows.title: Did that Colorado station sign really say gas for only $1.69? Yes, it did.
rows.standfirst: Fill-ups are even cheaper here than the falling national average. Here’s why.

rows.title: Do most Colorado homeowner’s policies offer full replacement value?
rows.standfirst: No. The Colorado Division of Insurance says fewer than 1 in 10 homeowner’s policies offer full replacement value if a home is destroyed.

rows.title: What’s Working: Office-bound jobs grew in Colorado in latest employment report
rows.standfirst: But declines elsewhere offset the gains in September and private-sector employers lost jobs. Plus: Unemployment rate improves to 4.1%, Colorado business rankings and more!

rows.title: How Colorado companies are dealing with Trump’s tariffs, including one that faced a $42 million bill
rows.standfirst: Colorado’s global imports fall, but export values are up as Trump tariffs continue to impact companies 8 months later.

rows.title: Colorado nearly 18 months late deciding pollution permit for Cargill meatpacking in Fort Morgan
rows.standfirst: Environmental group sues state for failing to act on an overdue pollution-caps permit for the slaughterhouse

rows.title: Steamboat Springs billionaire buys new apartment complex and slashes rent to help curb housing shortage
rows.standfirst: Venture capital investor and Steamboat Springs resident Mark Stevens acquired the 104-unit Riverview apartment complex for more than $95 million and offered units for well below market rates

rows.title: Colorado’s modular builders stand at a crossroads. Experts say more help is on the way.
rows.standfirst: Factory building could help make housing more affordable and available more quickly. But funding, regulatory clarity have been slow to come.

rows.title: Denver council rejects airport lease for ICE contractor Key Lime Air
rows.standfirst: The Denver City Council on Monday rejected a contract between Key Lime Air and Denver International Airport, citing the airline’s work transporting Immigration and Customs Enforcement detainees.

rows.title: US Patent Office picks Montana to replace former regional office in Denver
rows.standfirst: The agency made a speedy decision after asking for public input on where to put a new office.

rows.title: Federal judge blocks Colorado law requiring that consumers be warned of air quality effects of gas stoves
rows.standfirst: The judge agreed with an argument from the Association of Home Appliance Manufacturers, a trade group, that the law likely violates their First Amendment rights

rows.title: Uncertainty clouds Colorado state budget picture, as economy wobbles
rows.standfirst: The federal government shutdown delayed the release of key business and labor data, leaving forecasters in the dark about the true state of the economy

rows.title: What’s Working: Colorado’s talent pipeline report identifies 163 “top jobs”
rows.standfirst: Art directors, elevator repair workers and wind-turbine technicians all made the cut. Plus: Edgewater becomes first to change its tipped minimum wage, Denver inflation at 2.2% and the holidays.

rows.title: Democrats, local governments are gearing up for another round of battles over housing in Colorado
rows.standfirst: One of the bills, called the HOME Act, would make it easier for public schools and universities, local public housing authorities and certain nonprofit organizations to build residential units on their land

rows.title: Christmas trees are more expensive than ever in Colorado. What gives?
rows.standfirst: Yes, we live near vast forests of evergreen trees. But for purposes of decorating for the holiday, most of us are buying pines from far away.

rows.title: Labubus invade Denver airport, the first in the U.S. to showcase the weird — and weirdly popular — collectible
rows.standfirst: The creepy-cute plushy dolls, licensed from the pages of a kids’ picture book based on Nordic mythology, have become the hottest collectible in the world. You can now get one at Denver’s airport.

rows.title: Colorado communities argue the “just transition” from coal isn’t all that just
rows.standfirst: The Public Utilities Commission could revisit deals struck for cities and counties that were not in the room when deals were made to close holes left by coal-fired power plants and the mines that supply them

rows.title: Time is up for operators of a beloved Grand Junction farm market
rows.standfirst: The owners of Okagawa Farms say they’re ready to move on after 34 years and have put out a “for sale” sign on their operation fronting the Colorado River

rows.title: Colorado is feeling the effects of AI as legislative deadlock over regulation continues
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers return to the state Capitol in January to try for a fourth time to reach a deal on how to place guardrails around artificial intelligence

rows.title: As two other Colorado youth homeless shelters close, Urban Peak waitlist grows
rows.standfirst: The four-story homeless shelter for youth ages 12-24 opened a year a half ago and has had a waitlist since its first day

rows.title: Here comes another Xcel Energy rate hike. This time, the utility is asking to raise your gas bill.
rows.standfirst: Colorado consumer advocate says second rate-increase request in a quarter is testing the will of customers and the Public Utilities Commission

rows.title: Colorado laws taking effect in 2026 will impact everything from bison to renters
rows.standfirst: Colorado has about 20 new laws taking effect on Jan. 1

rows.title: Trump administration forces coal power plant in northwestern Colorado to continue operating
rows.standfirst: Craig Unit 1 was scheduled to close Wednesday, but federal energy officials claim there is a power emergency necessitating repair of the 45-year-old, broken-down plant
